title.narrative: Establishment of Solar-Powered EV Charging Stations in Ulaanbaatar City

description.narrative: Mongolia faces a severe air pollution challenge, particularly in its capital, Ulaanbaatar, where over half of the population endures some of the worlds most hazardous air quality levels. This environmental challengeis driven by both ambient (outdoor) and household (indoor) air pollution, with coal combustion being theprimary source. In winter, the burning of coal in traditional ger dwellings accounts for more than 80% of thecitys air pollution, leading to dangerously high concentrations of particulate matter (PM2.5).The health implications are dire. Ambient air pollution contributes to over 2,800 premature deaths annuallyand economic losses amounting to 905 billion MNT (approximately 2.4% of GDP). Household air pollution,primarily from coal-burning cookstoves, results in over 4,300 deaths each year and economic losses of 3.9trillion MNT (7 .6% of GDP)1. These figures underscore the urgent need for comprehensive interventions tomitigate air pollution and its associated health and economic burdens.Ulaanbaatar, the capital city of Mongolia, faces severe air pollution, particularly during the winter months.In 2022, the citys annual average PM2 .5 concentration was approximately 52.9 µg/m3, significantlyexceeding the World Health Organizations (WHO) recommended annual limit of 5 µg/m3 . On the mostpolluted days, PMz. 5 levels have reached as high as 337.9 µg/m3, nearly 68 times the WHO guideline.
